title: Fort Huachuca staging area and the regiment broken up
summary: The regiment was moved to Arizona to prepare for overseas, but the Battle of the Bulge brought orders that broke up the outfit and band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: We had a pretty good band, too, down there in Breckenridge. And that's the second band I was in. So after that, they were readying -- getting ready to go

overseas. Yeah, the regiment were getting ready to go overseas. So from Camp Breckenridge, Kentucky, we were shipped again on troop trains to (Fort) Huachuca, Arizona, which was a staging area. Staging area means that you're training and getting ready to go overseas, and when you're getting ready to go overseas you'd be surprised what it takes to send a division, a division -- a division is comprised of many regiments, and a regiment's got about 2,000 men, so you could see how many men. And if you bear in mind that there were 11 million people in the Armed Forces, 11 million. So we were shipped to Arizona, and when you're getting ready to be shipped overseas, that means they change everything you had. You get new clothes, new equipment. If you're in the infantry, you know, new weapons, new everything. When you get off the boat on the other side, everything you have is brand new. Yeah.

So then they started shipping them. So by this time -- now, the Colonel was really taking care of us. He loved musicians. He loved music. He liked to stand up and smoke his pipe and see his band parading down the street, you know. That old school, with the flag flying, you know, that sort of thing. And he just loved it and I loved him for loving it. And so then they got ready to make this move. Then the order came down from Headquarters -- Headquarters, Second Army, was in Texas. So then -- I could talk for three days about this, you know, details. So anyway, they found out that

-- then they began breaking up the -- our outfit was being broken up, you know, for -- this was when the war was at its worst. They had this big Battle of the Bulge incident. Then the order came down that no-one in the Armed Forces could move unless you were on the way to someplace. Wherever you are, stop, because everything's going to be turned around. So that broke up our band. It broke up the regiment and everything.

So then I remember I said to myself I was going to keep my nose clean and I wasn't going to -- least of all I wasn't going to get hurt, and I wasn't thinking about getting killed in nobody's army. So then I said now what'll I do? So we used to have -- in Huachuca, we used to call it -- the old post was an old National Guard post, and that's the post where Geronimo was captured by Captain White, in 1875, I think it was. That sort of thing. So there was a movie house up there, and these people had been living there, just like a little city, you know. And the (Unintelligible) down below was brand new, and it was all these barracks, and that's where the 92nd and 93rd colored divisions got trained. One went to Italy and one went to the Pacific. So by the time we got there we were the only outfit there, the 372nd Infantry.
